summary_paragraph: Mr. Meléndez, a man with chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and a history of heavy alcohol use, was admitted with acute right upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. His symptoms were attributed to alcoholic hepatitis and gastritis/duodenitis, with no evidence of gallbladder disease or pancreatitis. Liver enzymes and bilirubin were elevated on admission but improved during the hospital stay. Hypokalemia was corrected, and he was monitored for alcohol withdrawal without complications. His chest pain was consistent with stable angina, ruled out for acute cardiac injury. He was restarted on losartan for hypertension, educated on medication adherence, and discharged home with plans for shelter support and outpatient follow-up.
